Governance review

Who approves and who benefits

The Phoenix board has four equal seats. Three YES votes approve an action. Some payment recipients also took part in approving those payments.

What a removal would leave behind

If Vini were removed, the ERIS/Creda and Superbolt relationships would remain among the other directors. Vini is a recorded dissenting voice, but Rose also opposed Estima and voted NO on A272. At an unchanged 75% threshold, three equal remaining seats would still need all three YES votes. A reduction to 60% would let any two approve.

4853’s possible effects and the safeguards needed

The established public handle/address links place 0xphilipp in a Phoenix board seat, the Think Tank technical proposal role, the 50-of-90 ERIS multisig seat, the 4853 proposer/YES-voter role, an ERIS validator role and Treasury beneficiary/OTC relationships. Validators, contracts and large holders

Validator ballots differed

Galactic Punks, ERIS and Orbital Command voted YES. Smart Stake and Ceres voted VETO. HighStakes voted ABSTAIN. Eleven reviewed allocation-linked validators had no current ballot.

Only BackBone Labs and cosmosrescue among those unvoted validators had material current hub delegations.

The large vAMP account is unidentified

The 215,228-vAMP account remains unattributed. It holds Galactic Punks NFTs and received several direct Galactic Punks transfers, but their reward or payment classification is unresolved.

NFT holdings, transfers, timing and protocol usage do not establish common ownership.

Other paid contributors and counterparties

Recurring core, comms, ambassador and moderator recipients; grant recipients; OTC counterparties; operations contracts; and the ERIS protocol fee account also need payment and approval records. Contract and module accounts must not be mislabeled as people.

Vini and MB

Vini: audit beneficiary and overlapping signer

Vini proposed A249’s 16,900-USDC audit payment to Vini’s address and supplied one of its three deciding YES votes. The alleged earlier recusal agreement remains unverified; audit scope and independent acceptance still need review.

Vini’s board address is also a 10-weight ERIS signer. Vini rejected the earlier Estima A258 and supported the later two-contract migration-admin transfer to the Phoenix board. October’s new Stewardship schedules omitted Vini while separate infrastructure payments continued; the reason is unresolved.

MB: voting alignment and project relationships

MB voted YES on 251 of 252 proposals authored by 0xphilipp where MB cast a ballot. Many were routine operations; this is a reason to examine independent review, not proof of coordination.

The completed Treasury capture records 57,096 USDC to MB in its 2026 window. Two close-together claims represented separate entitlements. AADAO names MB as Superbolt’s representative; the full grant-to-distribution and delivery reconciliation remains open.

Monitored Vini and MB wallet histories remain truncated. These records do not establish lifetime income or the absence of other relationships. Other directors approved Estima’s original A266 grant without 0xphilipp; A272’s proposed removal and threshold reduction failed.

Three recipient wallets supplied the passing 75/100 YES weight. Phoenix A33 separately created four permanent locks with 21,600.000001 ampLUNA in total. This is Phoenix A33, not Lion DAO A33.

These are TLA voting locks, not native LUNA ballots. Current queries show fixed end periods for locks 429 and 432, with an additional 1 ampLUNA in 432. The change transactions and compliance with award terms remain unresolved; a changed state alone does not establish a breach.

Superbolt: three beneficiary YES votes

Neutron proposal 35 executed a 90,000-USDC batch on 5 August 2025: one 45,000-USDC payment and three 15,000-USDC payments. Its three recorded YES ballots came from three recipient wallets. This was collective approval, not a unilateral payment.

Separately, AADAO reports 80,000 dollars paid from an original 125,000-dollar Superbolt award, with 45,000 cancelled after rescoping. That upstream award has not been fully reconciled to the distribution. They are not additive funding, and neither amount is established as personal profit.
